blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 1
MAN NOT TO BE WORSHIPED
Scripture Text: Acts 14:1-18

In this quarter we continue to look at what God did in those saints of the Book of Acts, how they understood the teachings of Christ and the Apostles, and how they were led by the Holy Spirit. The results of these give us the pattern of the ideal Church of God that we have. We should ask ourselves, "How did those saints attain to these virtues?" The answer will give you the blueprint for your life, both personally and in the church.

It was so urgent that the early church take the Gospel to the world that no other need compared with it. Today with the critical condition of the world, closing doors to the Gospel, and the growing flood of evil covering the land, it is most urgent. These studies in Acts are not only to give us knowledge, but to add equipment for our task. What is not done today will not be done. The responsibility rests upon us.
MEMORY VERSE: Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve. —Matthew 4:10
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Corinthians 2:1-5 Preaching Christ in power.
Tue.—1 Corinthians 1:18-24 Christ, the wisdom of God.
Wed.—1 Thessalonians 2:9-13 Believing the message.
Thu.—1 Corinthians 9:15-23 Dedicated lives spread Gospel.
Fri.—Philippians 3:7-15 Knowledge of Christ is precious.
Devotional Reading: Matthew 28:16-20 The great commission.
They So Spake

Acts 14:1-3 Paul and Barnabas had been driven from Antioch by unbelievers. Undiscouraged, they continued preaching in Iconium. Here they followed their usual procedure. They went first to the Jewish synagogue and preached Christ. They so spake, that a great multitude . . . believed, both Jews and Greeks. As everywhere, the main body of Jews did not believe. These stirred up the Gentiles, poisoned their minds against the brethren. It is easier to tear down by evil stories than to build up by true teaching. Paul and Barnabas were not frightened. They continued speaking boldly in the Lord. God supported their words by empowering them to do signs and wonders—miracles. It was the word of his grace—the Word which He gave, the Word telling of the gift of Himself to man.

They so spoke that their preaching brought results. Their hearers believed. Here are some things we can learn from their preaching. Consider these points: (1) The theme was Jesus Christ, the crucified and risen Savior (1 Corinthians 2:2). (2) The Apostles believed the message (1Thessalonians 2:13). (3) They experienced the message (1 Corinthians 1:18). (4) They were dedicated to the spread of the message, not shunning suffering or death (1 Corinthians 9:15-16). (5) They humbled themselves and exalted Christ (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). (6) They preached in the power of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:4).

God's plan was that the Law should blossom into the Gospel. The people of the Law were to be led by it to Christ, then to go on to enjoy salvation through His Gospel. For this reason the Apostles went in each town first

to the people of the Law, or the Jews, who were expected to enter first into the open door. That they did not is tragic evidence on the hardness and blindness of the human heart.
Driven From Iconium

Acts 14:4-7 The fury of the Jews and the miracles of God were each powerful enough to gain a following. The city was divided. A strong force of people with their rulers assaulted the Apostles, meaning to stone them. Paul and Barnabas fled unto Lystra and Derbe where they preached the gospel.

Some things in the history in Acts stand out so continuously that we may overlook them like green in a landscape. One is the never-slackening zeal of the Apostles in preaching the Gospel. Another is the protecting hand of God upon them always. Imprisoned, threatened, beaten, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ. Driven from one town, they preached the Gospel boldly in the Lord in the next. That "in the Lord" is the secret. Why? Something within them resembled an unquenchable fire, and they desired to spread it to others. For us to adequately spread the Gospel as they did, we need to gain the driving force that these men had.
A Lame Man Healed

Acts 14:8-10 As Paul preached at Lystra, a lame man listened and believed. His feet were crippled. He never had walked. Paul perceived he had faith to be healed. He cried, Stand upright on thy feet. He did not stretch out his hand and ask for help. Without learning, the man leaped and walked.
Paul and Barnabas Refuse Worship

Acts 14:11-18 The people were heathen worshipers of false gods. Seeing the healing, they shouted, The gods are come down to us. They mistook the source of this supernatural power. What was already in their minds formed their thinking. They called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, Roman names of Greek gods who they thought had come down from Mount Olympus to bless them. The priest of Jupiter . . . brought oxen . . . and would have done sacrifice to them as gods. Let us never forget that there is much heathenism in America. Thousands of people neither attend church nor send their children to Sunday school. They look to good luck more than God's grace. When the Apostles realized what was taking place, they were horrified at the blasphemous worship. They rent their clothes—signifying great concern, and ran in—urgency, crying out— strong opposition. "Don't do this." We also are men of like passions—the same nature—with you. They were not gods, only men. What the people had said exalted men above their place and lowered God from His. The insult to God pained the Apostles. They immediately pointed to the living God, Creator of heaven . . . and all things. Similar praise was given to Herod. Herod accepted and gloried in the blasphemous praise. The Apostles rejected it with fear. The difference lay within their hearts. Herod, selfish and proud, sought his own glory. The Apostles desired God's glory. God punished Herod, but was pleased with the Apostles. The power of creation sets God infinitely above man who is created. Even in past times before Christ came to reveal God; God gave witness of Himself through His gifts of nature, rain, fruitful seasons, etc. Nature speaks to all the world of a good Heavenly Father. The heathen has this much revelation of God. Romans 1:19-25 describes the opportunity and the idolatry of people such as at Lystra. It was all the Apostles could do to restrain the people from sacrificing to them. Paul brought good tidings that they should turn from these vain things unto a living God.
JUST A THOUGHT
Carnal men love the praise of men. Godly men love the praise of God.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 2
PAUL STONED AT LYSTRA
Scripture Text: Acts 14:19-28

Persecution and tribulation may serve to strengthen the church. Whether it does or not depends on how persons react to it and how they use it. This is portrayed in this week's lesson, of which Acts 14:22 is the key.

Paul was now getting a taste of the bitter medicine he had spooned out to others in times past. He had been implicated in the stoning of Stephen. Paul was now suffering in behalf of the Gospel he had once persecuted. Once the people at Lystra wanted to worship these missionaries; then they stoned them. They experienced from one extreme to the other. But the power of the Spirit within the Apostles was more than equal to it.

Whether we know it or not, the world is watching our behavior closely. What will our attitude toward life's grueling situations mean to our children, our neighbors, and all those we are in contact with?
MEMORY VERSE: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. —Psalm 126:5
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Timothy 3 God's standard for placing men in office.
Tue.—James 1:12-22 True religion evidenced by conduct.
Wed.—James 5:7-12 The patience of the saints.
Thu.—1 Peter 3:8-22 The Christian and persecution.
Fri.—1 Peter 4:12-19 The Christian and suffering.
Devotional Reading: 1 Peter 4:1-11 Christian in Gospel Day.
Paul Encounters Persecution

Acts 14:19-20 The Jews of Antioch and Iconium followed Paul and Barnabas to Lystra. Prevented from stoning them in Iconium, they were determined to do it. They persuaded the people of Lystra—convinced them the Apostles were a menace. Together they stoned Paul and drew him out as dead. But God had more work for Paul. As the disciples stood round . . . he rose up—Paul recovered. They only supposed him to be dead, and he was probably unconscious. There is no thought of a miracle here. There can be no doubt that as the disciples stood watching their dear brother, they were praying, and God was watching. God raised him up. Paul came into the city, stayed overnight, and then with Barnabas went to Derbe where they preached the gospel. He did not go to the hospital or take a week to recuperate.
Why Go Back?

Acts 14:21-23 In Derbe they taught many. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch. What drew Paul and Barnabas back where they had been persecuted? It was love for their converts, who were among enemies of Christ. They needed establishing in Christ to continue to live victoriously. It was a shepherd's desire to feed and nourish and safeguard his flock. This is the biblical standard that must motivate all preaching and Sunday school teaching for it to be effective. They exhorted them to continue in the faith, to believe, trust, and

keep contact with God. Each of us has a duty to encourage, build up, and give spiritual food to others. Many newborn souls fall away because of neglect. If the planted Word is watered and cultivated, it will bear fruit. The devil places much tribulation in the way of those entering the Kingdom of God. Do not be turned aside by it.

Paul and Barnabas ordained . . . elders in every church. To give the young disciples guidance, the Apostles placed elders, spiritual leaders. They did this not in their own judgment, but prayed with fasting, getting God's leading. They did not leave the churches to be humanly ruled, but commended them to the Lord. The Apostles worked in the grace of God, free to follow Him, responsible to Him. The wisdom of this divine plan is seen in that they fulfilled their God-given task.

Some Words have been lifted from the Scripture and applied to systems of most formal and restricted ceremonies far removed from the free, Spirit-directed acts of the Apostles. When Paul and Barnabas ordained and confirmed, they were not setting formal patterns to be copied and conformed to. It was not ritual. When they rehearsed God's doings to the Antioch church, they were not making formal report to a governing board. In Christ, they were free from binding, human rules or ceremonies. They acted as the occasion arose and the Spirit led. God deals with the heart, the inner man. Any system that removes the essential action from the inside to the outside of man is robbing it of life.

The church shared in the joy of success as they gathered . . . together, and the Apostles rehearsed God's doings. A special cause for praise was the fact that Gentiles also were accepted by God into His church.
Paul and Barnabas had experienced the tears of sowing, but the joy of reaping repaid them abundantly. It repays in our day also. Read the Memory Verse again.

The best recipe for success: God-called, God-filled, God-led.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 3
A PROBLEM WITHIN THE CHURCH
Scripture Text: Acts 15:1-31

In Amos, heathen is the word used, in Acts, Gentiles. The words are often used interchangeably. Since Israel was God's chosen people and Gentiles were any people not Israelites, the name Gentiles came to mean people who are not God's people, or heathen.

We have studied the problem presented at the home of Cornelius. We also learned how the Holy Spirit helped Peter and the Apostles find the solution. Today we study of another problem presented to the leaders of the church at Jerusalem. Returning from their missionary journey, Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch. Then visitors coming from Judaea brought up a problem. Under the power of the Holy Spirit working through the hearts of these faithful men, God made plain to His servants His mind in the matter. The answer is that Christ was meant for the whole world, and God had just one way to accomplish this—a heart work.
MEMORY VERSE: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they. —Acts 15:11
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ephesians 4:1-16 The unity of the Spirit.
Tue— 1 Corinthians 6:9-20 Glorify God in your body.
Wed.—Ephesians 5:6-20 The works of light and darkness.
Thu.—John 10:31-42 Believe God.
Fri.—Luke 2:25-35 Simeon sees Light of the Gentiles.
Devotional Reading: John 8:31-47 True children of Abraham.
A Spirit of Opposition

Acts 15:1-5 The visiting brethren taught . . . Except ye be circumcised . . . ye cannot be saved. Discerning the tension, the church sent some, including Paul and Barnabas, to discuss the matter with the Apostles and elders at Jerusalem. Upon reaching Jerusalem, they encountered Pharisees, who were strict in keeping the Law of Moses. Paul and Barnabas opposed the restrictions of these "Judaizers" vigorously. They had observed hundreds of Gentiles transformed by the power of the Holy Spirit into Christians, who were fully equal in quality to the Jewish Christians. Both Paul and Barnabas were sure that the only thing needed to make a man fully acceptable to God was divine grace, and this was given Jews and Gentiles alike as a result of faith and nothing but faith in Christ.
Apostles Present Evidence

Acts 15:6-21 The apostles and elders came together to study the question. After much disputing, Peter gave his experience with Gentiles. God gave them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us. He put no difference between us and them. Yet Jews were circumcised and Gentiles were not. God purified their hearts by faith, not by circumcision. Why put a yoke upon the neck—bind a burden—which the Jews were not able to bear? Even if it had not been hard to keep the works of the Law, this could never have made them perfect.
© 2015 Church of God, Inc. A Problem Within the Church─ Lesson 3 www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 3
Peter concludes that all, both Jews and Gentiles, shall be saved only through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ.

Barnabas and Paul, like Peter, gave their experiences, not their opinions. As they had gone preaching, God had used them to save many Gentiles and to do miracles among them. This could not have been accomplished if all God's requirements had not been met.

James took the facts that had been given and connected them with prophecy (Amos 9:11-12), given about eight hundred years before. God promised to build again the tabernacle of David—figurative language meaning to raise up a means of salvation—and that the Gentiles would seek after the Lord. This was strong evidence. God promised to save Gentiles, and He had saved uncircumcised Gentiles. James reasoned from this that God did not require circumcision for salvation. Then why should men require it? Nothing further is required. He suggested the contents of a letter to be sent to the Gentile church at Antioch.

Were the Apostles in Jerusalem heads of the church with authority to rule in matters of doctrine? No. Let us examine and see that they did not rely on their own judgment. They considered (1) God's action in Peter's experience, (2) God's action in the experience of Paul and Barnabas, and (3) God's will as written in the Bible. When these agreed, they were confident that God had made known His decision. At no time did the Apostles legislate or make rules of doctrine. It was natural and right that the church consult with them as having more experience, having been with Jesus, and especially as having the gift of being Apostles. They submitted to the leadership of Spirit-led leaders.
The Plan Accepted

Acts 15:22-29 The apostles and elders, with the whole church—unity and equality—decided to send Judas and Silas, who were prophets (Acts 15:32), with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch with the letter. Seen here are a few distinguishing marks of the Church of God: (1) No man-made creed or discipline. (2) No human head of the church. (3) Unity of all in the church. Not all could go to Jerusalem. Not all could speak in the meeting. But all were interested, considered, and consulted. All rejoiced together in the way of the Lord. A difference in opinion does not necessarily mean a person is wrong in spirit.

It seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us—not man's decision, yet men joined in it—to lay upon you no greater burden . . . Circumcision would have been a needless burden. It, being a type of purity, was unnecessary when the reality of purity was obtained in Christ. Four things they, and we also, must keep from to remain pure: (1) Meats offered to idols. (2) Blood. The life . . . is in the blood (Leviticus 17:11-13). Reverence for life requires us to pour out the blood and not eat it. (3) Things strangled. Strangling would retain some blood. (4) Fornication. Spiritual and literal fornication is a sin of impurity and keeps one from the Kingdom of God (Exodus 20:14; 1 Corinthians 6:9-10). What is your idol?
The Church Rejoices

Acts 15:30-31 Reaching Antioch, the brethren gathered the multitude together. The message was for all the church. All were equal. Reading the letter, they rejoiced for the consolation—for the freedom of the Gospel, rejoiced that their salvation rested not in difficult keeping of outward forms and ordinances of the Law, but in inward connection with Jesus Christ and heart purity.

We no longer live under the Law of Moses. We are not saved by keeping outward forms, ceremonies of the Law, or ordinances such as circumcision. God saves a person by doing a work in the heart. When He puts His grace into a heart, that heart lives and is saved.
JUST A THOUGHT
It is what we learn after we know it all that really counts.

paragraphs.text: Were the Apostles in Jerusalem heads of the church with authority to rule in matters of doctrine? No. Let us examine and see that they did not rely on their own judgment. They considered (1) God's action in Peter's experience, (2) God's action in the experience of Paul and Barnabas, and (3) God's will as written in the Bible. When these agreed, they were confident that God had made known His decision. At no time did the Apostles legislate or make rules of doctrine. blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 4
A PROBLEM OVER JOHN MARK
Scripture Text: Acts 15:36-41

When Paul and Barnabas started on their second missionary journey, the question arose as to whether John Mark should accompany them. Paul said no; Barnabas said yes. This resulted in a sharp contention, and they separated. Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed for Cyprus, but Paul took Silas and went through Syria and Cilicia. John Mark needed to learn the lesson that we have to pay for our own mistakes and that to be a Christian takes courage. Paul was in a position to teach him those lessons, and he was the type of man who never flinched in the face of an unpleasant duty. Paul was right.

But Barnabas was also right. His talent was to reach out, draw in, and raise up young workers in the Gospel. Paul himself was one of those young workers and probably owed more to Barnabas than to any other human being for the place he filled now. Barnabas felt it dangerous to risk the loss of one such young life for lack of his encouragement. This was God's way for both Paul and Barnabas to go to work wholeheartedly for Him. Mark was later restored to usefulness.
MEMORY VERSE: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily. —Acts 16:5
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ephesians 1:15-23 Pray for wisdom and knowledge.
Tue.—Romans 8:1-17 Life in the Spirit.
Wed.—Romans 12:9-21 Christian conduct.
Thu.—Hebrews 12:12-29 Christian endurance.
Fri.—Luke 12:35-48 Be a faithful servant.
Devotional Reading: Colossians 3:1-17 True center of life.
A Difference Arises

Acts 15:36-38 When the mission of the letter was complete, Paul, Barnabas, and Silas remained in Antioch for a time. It was a large, spiritual, active, and growing church. It was a good place for them to work and gain spiritual nourishment. But this could not go on for long. Paul had tasted of pioneer work out where they had never heard of Jesus. Restless to return where God called him and desiring to know how their converts did, He said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren . . . where we have preached. The plan suited Barnabas. The warm nature of the fatherly Barnabas gave him a further thought—to take with them John, his relative (John Mark). But Paul thought not good to take him. Why not? Because he had departed from them on the previous trip (Acts 13:5, 13). Why take the risk again?

For two men, both filled with the Spirit and undoubtedly loving each other, to differ so sharply means each had strong reasons. They faced a hard way, dangerous travels, and many enemies. Endurance, both physical and spiritual, was needed. Their burden was to win lost souls to Christ. John Mark had once quit. Paul thought it dangerous to risk the failure of their mission by taking along a quitter. Barnabas showed a great concern over the risk of losing the young John Mark for lack of his encouragement.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 4
The Separation

Acts 15:39-41 The contention was so sharp . . . that they departed asunder one from the other. The contention in this instance meant a statement or point that one argues for a true and valid position. Each was determined he was acting in the will of God and would not yield. Barnabas took Mark and took ship to Cyprus. That island was Barnabas' old home. He and Paul had begun their first missionary journey here.

Paul chose Silas. They were recommended by the brethren—commended to the charge of the grace of God. Committing them into God's hands, into His life and power— this was the best possible help and protection. Here we see a token of the church's confidence in all four of these brethren. Departing, Paul and Silas went through Syria and Cilicia —where Paul and Barnabas had been on their first journey. Cilicia was Paul's home area. Here we begin to see the hand of God in the moves. They went confirming the churches, not a formal ceremony. By preaching the Word and living the life, they strengthened, or confirmed, these people to continue living in the Lord.

Anger, selfishness, and malice did not enter into this contention. Paul and Barnabas could not have continued under the blessing and power of God as they did, had they fallen into these sins. Paul showed his approval of the hard work of Barnabas in his reference to him in 1 Corinthians 9:6. We find no taint of resentment in John Mark. No, we cannot point to Paul and Barnabas as an excuse for animosity and quarreling. Anger, resentment, and revenge are sinful. Saved people can differ in opinion and judgment.
Having Confidence

Sometimes one feels that these Bible people were a little above the human, that they occupied a place we cannot reach, or had spiritual gifts greater than God would give us. This incident is written to show us that this is not true.

John Mark needed to learn the lesson that we have to pay for our own mistakes and that to be a Christian takes courage. Paul was in a position to teach him those lessons, and he was the type of man who never flinched in the face of an unpleasant duty. But Barnabas was right too. This lovable man, who all through the New Testament stands out as one who was constantly doing someone kindness, was just the type of man to take young John Mark in hand and give him the kindly treatment he needed. Paul administered the rod on young John Mark, and he was right; the boy needed that. But he also needed kindly understanding, and this his friend, Barnabas furnished him. John Mark lost Paul's confidence by leaving them once, but that confidence was later restored. Some years later, we find references to Mark made by Paul and others which indicate that Mark was a good soldier for Christ. Read Colossians 4:10-11; 2 Timothy 4:11. Mark became the author of one of our Gospel Books. Paul's severity and the kindly understanding of Barnabas combined to make possible the stability of Mark's life.

"Did you hear about Paul? I thought he was saved. But if he were, how could he deal so with Barnabas and Mark?" Sound familiar? Brother and Sister do not be too quick to lose confidence. We need not always understand motives. Our brother may see differently than we. He may be closer to God than we. We read of no repentance being necessary in this incident.

We live today in an age which too often takes sides with Barnabas against Paul. Parents today are prone to settle every dispute with their children on the basis of compromise and loving understanding. We need some of Paul's sternness in modern domestic life. When young people make mistakes, they need to learn that eventually they themselves have to pay for these mistakes. Parents are foolish to try to relieve children of this payment, and such children themselves grow up to be spoiled worldlings if their parents pass over every mistake and failure and forsaking of responsibility, attributing them all to the immaturity of youth.

Departing, Paul and Silas went through Syria and Cilicia —where Paul and Barnabas had been on their first journey. Cilicia was Paul's home area. Here we begin to see the hand of God in the moves. They went confirming the churches, not a formal ceremony. By preaching the Word and living the life, they strengthened, or confirmed, these people to continue living in the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Anger, selfishness, and malice did not enter into this contention. Paul and Barnabas could not have continued under the blessing and power of God as they did, had they fallen into these sins. Paul showed his approval of the hard work of Barnabas in his reference to him in 1 Corinthians 9:6. We find no taint of resentment in John Mark. No, we cannot point to Paul and Barnabas as an excuse for animosity and quarreling. Anger, resentment, and revenge are sinful. Saved people can differ in opinion and judgment.

paragraphs.text: Sometimes one feels that these Bible people were a little above the human, that they occupied a place we cannot reach, or had spiritual gifts greater than God would give us. This incident is written to show us that this is not true.

paragraphs.text: John Mark needed to learn the lesson that we have to pay for our own mistakes and that to be a Christian takes courage. Paul was in a position to teach him those lessons, and he was the type of man who never flinched in the face of an unpleasant duty. But Barnabas was right too. This lovable man, who all through the New Testament stands out as one who was constantly doing someone kindness, was just the type of man to take young John Mark in hand and give him the kindly treatment he needed. Paul administered the rod on young John Mark, and he was right; the boy needed that. But he also needed kindly understanding, and this his friend, Barnabas furnished him. John Mark lost Paul's confidence by leaving them once, but that confidence was later restored. Some years later, we find references to Mark made by Paul and others which indicate that Mark was a good soldier for Christ. Read Colossians 4:10-11; 2 Timothy 4:11. Mark became the author of one of our Gospel Books. Paul's severity and the kindly understanding of Barnabas combined to make possible the stability of Mark's life.

paragraphs.text: "Did you hear about Paul? I thought he was saved. But if he were, how could he deal so with Barnabas and Mark?" Sound familiar? Brother and Sister do not be too quick to lose confidence. We need not always understand motives. Our brother may see differently than we. He may be closer to God than we. We read of no repentance being necessary in this incident.

paragraphs.text: We live today in an age which too often takes sides with Barnabas against Paul. Parents today are prone to settle every dispute with their children on the basis of compromise and loving understanding. We need some of Paul's sternness in modern domestic life. When young people make mistakes, they need to learn that eventually they themselves have to pay for these mistakes. Parents are foolish to try to relieve children of this payment, and such children themselves grow up to be spoiled worldlings if their parents pass over every mistake and failure and forsaking of responsibility, attributing them all to the immaturity of youth.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 5
PHILIPPI RECEIVES THE GOSPEL
Scripture Text: Acts 16:1-15

This disagreement of Paul and Barnabas resulted in two teams going to visit churches. In our lesson today we follow the movement of Paul and Silas. They revisited some churches where Paul had preached. They went into what is now called Asia Minor, but the Holy Spirit had reason to forbid the Word to be preached in Asia. They were obedient to the leading of the Spirit.

Paul, in a vision, was directed to Macedonia. They preached in Philippi. Lydia and her household believed the Word. Here we have the reason why the Holy Spirit did not allow Paul to preach in Asia. There was a bigger work to be done in Europe. This is the first time the Gospel had been preached in Europe. From Macedonia, the Gospel was carried up into central and northern Europe and hence to America and around the world.
MEMORY VERSE: I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will guide thee with mine eye. —Psalm 32:8
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—James 3:13-18 True and false wisdom.
Tue.—Isaiah 55:6-13 Prosperity in godly work.
Wed.—Proverbs 11:12-23 Reward in sowing righteousness.
Thu.—Micah 6:8-16. Futility of sowing wickedness.
Fri.—Proverbs 10:23-32 The wise sow righteousness.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 126 Happiness in work of God.
Timothy's Opportunity

Acts 16:1-5 Revisiting Derbe and Lystra with Silas, Paul finds Timotheus (Greek for Timothy). He was a disciple of Christ, and the son of Eunice (see 2 Timothy 1:5), a Jewess, who, with her mother Lois, was probably saved under Paul's preaching on his first visit some years before. Probably Timothy was saved then also, for Paul calls him my own son in the faith (1Timothy 1:2). His father was a Greek. To avoid opposition from Jews, Paul circumcised Timothy—not to save Timothy, but to gain the hearing of the Jews.

To go with Paul, hear him preach, see him work, and to work with him was a great opportunity and the best training Timothy could have had. To work with godly preachers, teachers, and workers, learning from them, having fellowship with them, is training of the greatest value. This, coupled with prayer and study, would produce some sorely needed great Gospel workers.
The Holy Spirit Closes One Way

Acts 16:6-8 Paul and company meant to visit points in Asia. The Holy Spirit forbade this. Obeying, they came down to Troas. Troas was the farthest western point in Asia. They were at their journey's end. They now needed special divine guidance to know where to go to preach. God had closed all doors without opening any new ones.

LESSON 5

While the Apostles' plans and God's plans coincided, the Spirit said nothing, silently guiding. When they differed, He spoke, first, to forbid remaining in Asia, then, to lead into Europe. He will use His power in our lives also. When He lives in a heart, He brings direction.
The Holy Spirit Opens Another Way

Acts 16:9-12 Waiting in Troas for God's direction, Paul received a vision. There stood a man of Macedonia, who said, Come over into Macedonia and help us. Paul knew this was God's Word directing him. They obeyed. It appears that Luke, the author of Acts, joined the company at Troas, for now for the first time he writes "we" in verses 10-12.

If God had not closed all other doors and then given Paul a vision, it is likely that he would never have gone into Europe. He would no doubt have concentrated his efforts on the churches of Asia. Sometimes God has a bigger work for us than we realize. Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course . . . to Neapolis. They lost no time in starting out. Neapolis was in Macedonia. And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city . . . of Macedonia . . . And we were in that city abiding certain days. There being no synagogue, they would have to find some other means of reaching the people. Conditions were so much different in this city that they had to spend some time in getting acquainted with conditions and planning their tactics.
Lydia Receives the Gospel

Acts 16:13-15 In Philippi they attended a meeting of women by a river side. And a certain woman named Lydia . . . which worshipped God heard us. Lydia was worshiping God, no doubt, to the best of the light she had. When the Apostles spoke, the Lord opened her heart. She listened, accepted, and obeyed. She was baptized in water as Jesus commanded (Matthew 28:19; Mark 16:16) and as a symbol of her new birth. Note that her household, or family, were also saved, a tribute to her godly influence. She invited Paul and his brethren to stay in her home. She made them welcome to stay and preach the Gospel there.

It would seem that even back then, the women were more faithful in attending prayer meeting than were the men. So the work in Philippi started among the women who attended the prayer service. The mightiest thing done in Europe that day was when the Apostle slipped out in the early morning to a meeting place beneath the blue sky, by the side of the rushing stream, and there talked to the handful of women about the Savior of men's souls, Jesus Christ.
True worshipers of God know when they hear the Truth, and they respond to it. Those who only pretend to worship are apt to become heated from anger when they are faced with Gospel Truth.
God's Program

God has a program for His church. He has a better plan than man can form. It is a program, the details of which no one can guess. They must be revealed by the Spirit. No one could have guessed or reasoned out His plan to take the Gospel to Europe rather than farther into Asia. His plan is a simple plan, as we see in our lesson. It does not fit well with man's forms and pomp and earthly ambitions. If we drop our organizations and ceremonies and seek His way, He will reveal it.

Had Paul depended upon himself and closed his heart to the Spirit's voice, he would never have known his loss. He obeyed and waited for further leadings, and God richly fulfilled his expectations. We reap the benefits today.
JUST A THOUGHT
When the Spirit says NO, listen for His YES.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 6
PAUL MEETS A DEMON-POSSESSED WOMAN
Scripture Text: Acts 16:16-24

God had led Paul and Silas to Philippi in Europe. But not all was smooth sailing. The devil also was there to challenge their work. A soothsayer followed the Apostles. This is one who tells of future events or hidden knowledge by the help of unseen powers—a fortune teller. She advertised the preachers and their message. Paul, in Jesus' name, cast the demon out of the woman. The masters of the soothsayer imprisoned Paul and Silas. They were placed in stocks, a wooden frame with holes in which the feet were confined for punishment. What made the girl's action wrong? We can find the answer to this question in the Scripture. There is only one sure defense against the power of Satan. God commands us to have nothing to do with demons or their works.
MEMORY VERSE: Regard not them that have familiar spirits, neither seek after wizards, to be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God. —Leviticus 19:31
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—1 Peter 1:1-16 Present blessings.
Tue.—1 Peter 1:17-25 Future blessings.
Wed.—Ephesians 1:15-23 Prayer for wisdom, knowledge.
Thu.—John 4:1-14 Living water within.
Fri.—1 Corinthians 1:17-31 God chooses to use lowly things.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 2 Blessings of life in Christ.
Free Advertisement

Acts 16:16-17 As we went to prayer . . . Paul's company was staying at Lydia's house. They were going to a prayer meeting, perhaps at the meeting place by the riverside. A damsel—unmarried girl—met them. She did soothsaying for money. She could do this because she was possessed with a spirit of divination—a demon who could tell secret things. She followed the Apostles, shouting an announcement that the men were servants of the most high God, and showing the way of salvation.

LESSON 6
Present-Day Witchcraft

This evil is not a thing of the past only, for we have it today. In many forms it is present all around us. Superstition, belief in signs, spiritualism, Ouija boards, fortune telling, voodoo, hex, casting spells, doctoring by charms and magic formulas, trances, séances, work of mediums, and demon possession—all are parts of the same evil system. It is the devil trying to gain control of the souls of men, women, and children. It is dangerous to venture into his territory, however harmless it may appear at first. The devil is stronger than men. We cannot in our own strength be a match for him. There is a one hundred percent effective defense. It is the power of the Holy Spirit.
The Power of the Holy Spirit

Acts 16:18 Paul was patient, but after many days he became grieved and commanded the evil spirit in the name of Jesus Christ—the only One with authority and power over him—to come out of her. And he came out.
Jesus has power over demons (Luke 4:35-36), He gave His twelve Apostles power over them (Matthew 10:1), and He promised this power to His church (Mark 16:17).
Some Things to Learn About Demons

(1) Demons are evil spirits that can live in people. They are persons. This one is referred to as "he." (2) They are intelligent beings, having greater knowledge and insight than humans. This one knew who Paul and the others were, what their business was, and the truth of their message. (3) They can take control and possess humans. (4) They are of different kinds, as of divination, of infirmity, dumb spirits, and many others, but always evil. (5) Only God's power can cast out demons. (6) Only God's power can protect us from demons and their works.
Suffering for Christ

Acts 16:19-24 When her masters saw . . . The girl was not free. Bound by a demon and also bound to human masters, her slavery was of the worst kind. Now she was free, and the hope of their gains—in money— was gone. Angered, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them . . . unto the rulers. They accused them of (1) being Jews, the subject nation, (2) troubling the city, and (3) teaching customs contrary to Roman law.

The accusations stirred up the multitude that turned against the Apostles. Public opinion influenced the rulers. They rent off the clothes of Paul and Silas and ordered beating. Many stripes, marked by blood and pain were laid upon them. Not satisfied, they cast them into prison. The jailer, obeying an order to keep them safely, as one would dangerous criminals, thrust them—roughly—into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks. What Paul had done was according to God's Law and with God's help, but these innocent men had to suffer for their actions.

The aims of the church and the aims of the world are opposed. They belong to kingdoms directly opposite each other. For this reason the activity and success of the church brings persecution from the world. It did for Paul and Silas. But as they suffered in the body, they had joy within. They were hurting on the outside, but feeling good on the inside. They still had spiritual victory, as we shall see. To serve Jesus, we, too, will have to suffer for Him.

Read the Memory Verse. We are not to seek after wizards. Dabbling in these things, one is in danger of becoming demon possessed. This is God's Word with authority above any other word, whether of a government or group or individual.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 7
A NIGHT IN A PHILIPPIAN JAIL
Scripture Text: Acts 16:25-34

Last week's lesson left Paul and Silas in prison, with backs beaten and feet in stocks. At night in prison and in pain, Paul and Silas prayed and sang. God freed them by an earthquake. The jailer was about to commit suicide, but by the power of conviction of the Holy Spirit, he asked how to be saved. The Apostles taught him to believe in Jesus Christ. The jailer and his family believed and were baptized. They all enjoyed a meal and fellowship. The rulers released Paul and Silas from jail.

In this is shown the power promised to be given with the coming of the Holy Spirit. This power was in their hearts. The natural, human disposition under such circumstances would be anger, bitterness at the injustice, complaint, despair, and giving up. Their joy, hope, praise, and loyalty to God and His work came from an inside work of the Holy Spirit in their hearts. The same is our privilege too.
MEMORY VERSE: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. —Acts 16:31
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Romans 8:16-28 Suffering compared with glory.
Tue.—Hebrews 11:23-40 Reproach of Christ great riches.
Wed.—James 5:1-12 The patience of the saints.
Thu.—Matthew 5:1-16 Suffering lets our light shine.
Fri.—1 Peter 5:1-11 Christian life in God's care.
Devotional Reading: I Peter 2:11-25 Christ our great example.
Praises Bring an Earthquake

Acts 16:25-26 At midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises. In pain, unjustly imprisoned, the future uncertain, they praised God. It was from that within, not without. The prisoners heard. It must have sounded very strange in that dark, damp, musty prison to hear praises to God. But God heard also. He sent a sudden earthquake. The foundations shook, and all locks were broken—doors, stocks, chains, and whatever. It was His answer to their prayer. This did not just happen. It was brought to pass by God. Why? Because these men were prepared to glorify God through obedient, holy lives. By keeping alert to the Spirit's voice, they made themselves available to God. They prayed, and God sent the results. It was God's work. They did not produce the earthquake or persuade the jailer. It was the power of the Holy Spirit. They were only yielded tools. They just relaxed and watched God work.
The Great Question

Acts 16:27-30 The sleeping jailer heard it and awoke in fear. Jailers were put to death for allowing their prisoners to escape (Acts 12:19). He was about to commit suicide when Paul's voice startled him. Do thyself no

harm: for we are all here. The rare action of prisoners staying when free to go showed a supernatural power. Perhaps this, with something Paul had said, and the nearness he had come to death unprepared to meet God, caused conviction—a sense of his sin—to take hold of him. Urgently, he called for a light, and sprang in . . . trembling . . . fell down. He brought them out. Then—Sirs, what must I do to be saved? Nothing else mattered now.
The Gospel Message Is the Answer

Acts 16:31-32 Paul and Silas had the only answer. Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ—cast yourself upon Him, trust Him to do for you what you cannot do for yourself. Believe He is the One Who can and will. They opened the word of the Lord, not to the jailer only, but to all that were in his house.

The instruction to believe included all that always goes with real belief—(1) repentance of sin, (2) a turning from sin, (3) receiving of Christ as Savior, (4) obedience to God in holy living, (5) baptism as a symbol of one's change, and (6) restitution for past wrongs.

In the midst of turmoil in his life, Paul never forgot the essential purpose of his calling from God. It was to bear Christ's name and to be His witness unto all men. He was always ready to teach one or many how to be saved. His teaching was plain and unmixed with nonessentials. Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. This is still the message of the church. Keep it foremost, out in front of all activities and programs.
The Keeper Shows Sign of Change

Acts 16:33-34 He took Paul and Silas the same hour of the night—no waiting. He showed zeal. Washed their stripes—this was love. This was the fruit of repentance. He wanted to do all possible to right wrongs. Even though he may not have done the beating, he wanted to do whatever he could to make amends and ease the pain. Then he was baptized . . . and all his. They all believed on Christ, so all were baptized. The family was not saved by the jailer's believing, but by their own, as all must be. Straightway—without waiting even for the morning. Then he brought them into his house—suggesting they had been out where there was water for immersion. In his house, he set meat (food) before them. They finished the night eating and having fellowship together. Paul and Silas rejoiced with the jailer and his family in their new lives.

Conversion makes a change in the heart which shows on the outside. The jailer showed his conviction by his urgency and his trembling, which revealed a strong stirring of need. We see signs of repentance in his sincere actions toward the Apostles. This was something a man of his social position would never do. Another indication of his new birth is his willingness and desire to be baptized immediately. Another is his joy. Salvation always brings joy. The Spirit-filled person has joy, thanksgiving, and praise in his heart in spite of outward trouble. Inward salvation is indicated by a change in one's outward life. Our message is that Jesus saves all who believe in Him. The Spirit-filled person is only a channel through which God can move, a tool which He can use to do His work. God will use us if we yield to His leading.
JUST A THOUGHT
Almost everything can be bought at a reduced price except lasting peace and satisfaction.

The instruction to believe included all that always goes with real belief—(1) repentance of sin, (2) a turning from sin, (3) receiving of Christ as Savior, (4) obedience to God in holy living, (5) baptism as a symbol of one's change, and (6) restitution for past wrongs.
In the midst of turmoil in his life, Paul never forgot the essential purpose of his calling from God.
It was to bear Christ's name and to be His witness unto all men.
He was always ready to teach one or many how to be saved.
His teaching was plain and unmixed with nonessentials.
Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ.
This is still the message of the church.
Keep it foremost, out in front of all activities and programs.
Acts 16:33-34 He took Paul and Silas the same hour of the night—no waiting.
He showed zeal.
Washed their stripes—this was love.
This was the fruit of repentance.
He wanted to do all possible to right wrongs.
Even though he may not have done the beating, he wanted to do whatever he could to make amends and ease the pain.
Then he was baptized . . . and all his.
They all believed on Christ, so all were baptized.
The family was not saved by the jailer's believing, but by their own, as all must be.
Straightway—without waiting even for the morning.
Then he brought them into his house—suggesting they had been out where there was water for immersion.
In his house, he set meat (food) before them.
They finished the night eating and having fellowship together.
Paul and Silas rejoiced with the jailer and his family in their new lives.
Conversion makes a change in the heart which shows on the outside.
The jailer showed his conviction by his urgency and his trembling, which revealed a strong stirring of need.
We see signs of repentance in his sincere actions toward the Apostles.
This was something a man of his social position would never do.
Another indication of his new birth is his willingness and desire to be baptized immediately.
Another is his joy.
Salvation always brings joy.
The Spirit-filled person has joy, thanksgiving, and praise in his heart in spite of outward trouble.
Inward salvation is indicated by a change in one's outward life.
Our message is that Jesus saves all who believe in Him.
The Spirit-filled person is only a channel through which God can move, a tool which He can use to do His work.
God will use us if we yield to His leading.
Almost everything can be bought at a reduced price except lasting peace and satisfaction.

lessons.title: A NIGHT IN A PHILIPPIAN JAIL

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 8
APOSTLES TURN THE WORLD UPSIDE DOWN
Scripture Text: Acts 17:1-15

Leaving Philippi by request of the city officials, Paul and Silas left the nucleus of a healthy church behind them. The next stop of Paul and companions was at Thessalonica. Preaching in Thessalonica gained a great multitude of converts. Unbelieving Jews raised an uproar and seized Jason. The brethren sent Paul and Silas to Berea by night, where they continued preaching. The Bereans searched the Scriptures. The Jews from Thessalonica came there also and raised opposition. The brethren sent Paul to Athens.

The Bible is God's means of giving us the Truth. It is the best means of spreading the Gospel. Jesus said, ". . . the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life" (John 6:63). Nothing can make up for lack of the Bible in our teaching. It has authority, truth, and power.
MEMORY VERSE: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to everyone that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. —Romans 1:16
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Psalm 127 The vanity of work without God.
Tue.—Matthew 10:26-33 The value of life.
Wed.—Matthew 5:38-48 Neighbors and enemies.
Thu.—Psalm 119:161-168 Peace in keeping God's Law.
Fri.—Matthew 10:34-42 The reward of the righteous.
Devotional Reading: Matthew 10:16-25 Facing persecution.
A Good Workman

Acts 17:1-4 Paul and Silas came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews. And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them. Paul seemed most skillful at starting his preaching in a synagogue. The presence of one in Thessalonica, no doubt, had some influence on his stop there. This was their meeting place. He seems to have followed the line of Christ's reasoning on the Emmaus road when He said, "Ought not Christ to have suffered . . . and to enter into his glory?"—His death and resurrection (Luke 24:26-27). Jesus beginning at Moses and all the prophets . . . expounded . . . in all the scriptures the things concerning himself. These Old Testament Scriptures of Christ's necessary death for sin and His resurrection Paul used to prove that Jesus is Christ, because He fulfilled the prophecies about Him. Some Jews believed, and a great multitude of Greeks or Gentiles.
Power to Turn the World Upside Down

Acts 17:5-9 Those Jews not taken hold of by belief were taken hold of by envy. They gathered lewd fellows of the baser sort —wicked, lawless, bad, low-down, dishonorable, and worthless. In this they revealed their
© 2015 Church of God, Inc. Apostles Turn the World Upside Down─ Lesson 8 www.GodsAcres.org
SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 8

own character. They set all the city on an uproar against the Apostles. The mob assaulted the house where Paul and Silas stayed. Not finding them, they seized their host, Jason and others and took them before the rulers. They said Paul and Silas had turned the world upside down. What a strong testimony to these great men's lives! They accused the saints of treason—setting up Jesus as king, in place of Caesar. Disturbed, the rulers released Jason and the others on bail—security.

The Thessalonicans made the mistake so many make. They thought the Apostles meant the Kingdom of Jesus is an earthly one. Jesus' reign is spiritual and competes with no kingdom but Satan's, which it will destroy. See John 18:36; 1 John 3:8; Revelation 20:10.

How we see things depends upon our position. Being wrong, the mob saw the change in the world as wrong. The point of importance is that the Gospel will change the world wherever it touches it. The Gospel will not leave people as they are. The Apostles' preaching stirred either dedication or opposition. When Paul preached, he was usually driven out of town, but he left behind a changed people. The town was turned upside down. If we are to turn things around, we must preach and live the unadulterated Gospel of Christ without fear of the opposition of the world. We must dedicate ourselves wholly to God and move as He leads us. No other way will do.
Testing Paul's Message

Acts 17:10-12 The brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas. Paul and Silas do not seem to have been anxious. The church was anxious for them and sent them by night —secretly—unto Berea. In Berea Paul and Silas went into the synagogue. They just could not learn to avoid trouble by keeping still about Jesus. Results were different here than in Thessalonica. These had less prejudice and more honesty. These Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind—with an open mind, yet not a mind to believe just everything. They searched the scriptures daily to learn the truth or falsity of the Apostles' teaching. Therefore— because of their searching—many . . . believed. Reading of the Old Testament proved the teaching true and settled them more solidly in the faith than Paul's words alone could have done.

The Bereans wished neither to accept a lie nor to reject the Truth. There was one way to prove the matter. They read the Bible—the Old Testament; the New Testament was not yet written—to see if it said of Christ what Paul said. When they believed, they had the answer. If we base our belief in the Bible, we will not wonder and question. We can know the Truth if we so desire. The radio, books, and pulpits teach so many differing things. Study the Bible and try the teachings by it. Carry your Bible to church and try the sermon. Read it daily and prepare yourself. The majority of church people know little about the teachings of the Bible. A Bible-reading church is a strong church. A Bible-reading saint is unlikely to drift into false worship.
Followed to Berea

Acts 17:13-15 The peaceful condition was not allowed to continue. The unbelieving Jews of Thessalonica heard the news and came to Berea to destroy the Gospel growth there. They stirred up the people against Paul and Silas. Yet again, the brethren supplied the caution for Paul. To protect him, they took him to Athens. To throw off the pursuers, they pretended to start to the sea. Silas and Timothy stayed at Berea, but Paul sent word back to them to come to him quickly. There was urgent work of evangelizing to do.

One of the greatest mistakes Christians make is to present their personal opinions. The greatest contribution made by Reformation leaders was the position they took that Christian belief and conduct must be based wholly upon Scripture, and that nothing can be set forth as a directive for Christian conduct unless it be commanded or allowed by the Word of God. As we meet the contentions of skepticism, paganism, and of many sects and "isms", let us forbear to argue; instead, let us go back to the Scripture and measure what men say against what God has said.

paragraphs.text: How we see things depends upon our position. Being wrong, the mob saw the change in the world as wrong. The point of importance is that the Gospel will change the world wherever it touches it. The Gospel will not leave people as they are. The Apostles' preaching stirred either dedication or opposition. When Paul preached, he was usually driven out of town, but he left behind a changed people. The town was turned upside down. If we are to turn things around, we must preach and live the unadulterated Gospel of Christ without fear of the opposition of the world. We must dedicate ourselves wholly to God and move as He leads us. No other way will do.

paragraphs.text: One of the greatest mistakes Christians make is to present their personal opinions. The greatest contribution made by Reformation leaders was the position they took that Christian belief and conduct must be based wholly upon Scripture, and that nothing can be set forth as a directive for Christian conduct unless it be commanded or allowed by the Word of God. As we meet the contentions of skepticism, paganism, and of many sects and "isms", let us forbear to argue; instead, let us go back to the Scripture and measure what men say against what God has said.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 9
PAUL AT ATHENS
Scripture Text: Acts 17:16-34

For safety from persecuting Jews, the brethren had brought Paul from Berea to Athens, where he waited for Silas and Timothy to join him. This city was the chief seat of Grecian learning and civilization during the golden period of the history of Greece. Plato and Aristotle had lived and taught at Athens. The atmosphere of learning developed a people who desired to understand everything through human reasoning. To hear or tell some new thing became their purpose in life. This led to a shallow spiritual condition.

The idolatry in Athens caused Paul to be burdened, and he was ready to preach the Gospel to all who would listen. The philosophers asked Paul to speak to them of his doctrine. Paul spoke on "The Unknown God." Some believed.
MEMORY VERSE: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands. —Acts 17:24
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 4:19-26 Worship God in Spirit and Truth.
Tue.—Matthew 15:1-9 Vain worship.
Wed.—Acts 24:1-16 Worship through belief.
Thu.—Revelation 22:6-12 Angels not to be worshiped.
Fri.—Romans 1:18-26 Worship that leads to servitude.
Devotional Reading: Psalm 22:22-31 Sing gratitude to God.
What Do These Strange Things Mean?

Acts 17:16-21 Paul waited, but he could not wait for long. He saw Athens wholly given to idolatry and his spirit was stirred in him—he had a burden to change it. It was the stirring of the Holy Spirit. Therefore— because of the stir— he disputed with the Jews and devout persons and any who cared to meet with him. These shallow-minded philosophers were interested in the newness of Paul's message rather than its trueness. Jesus they supposed to be another god, one unknown to them but on the same level as their idols. With little or no feeling of need, but only a desire to satisfy their pride of keeping up on knowledge, they invited Paul to speak to them concerning this new doctrine that was strange to them. They wanted to know what these things mean. The message of Jesus and the Resurrection sounds strange in our modern day to those who have only a fleshly mind and nothing in the heart pertaining to true worship. Jesus is still an unknown god to the many idol worshipers of our land. Paul preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection. This is the message for the idolatry in our cities and was Paul's one subject.

Because Paul's spirit had tasted of the goodness of God, it was stirred at the sight of wickedness. Since Paul held God supreme, he could not bear to see idols usurping God's place. Does wickedness stir us? Can we listen indifferently to insult God and His Word? Does the spread of sin and idolatry in our land give us pain?

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 9
Paul Begins His Sermon

Acts 17:22-25 Ye are too superstitious. They trusted in false powers and useless practices. Paul used as an introduction an inscription on a local altar, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD, put there perhaps by those fearing the wrath of some neglected deity.

Uncivilized people receive the Gospel more readily than highly civilized ones. Athens' culture was her curse. It gave her a sense of self-sufficiency. History shows that when education, culture, science, and machinery enter a country ahead of the Bible, the hearts of the people lose in simplicity and become hardened to the Gospel. The greatest kindness we can show any people is to introduce them to the Truth of God's Word at our first opportunity.

God is a Spirit and dwelleth not in temples made with hands. The gifts He wants are not material things. The treasures He craves are a broken and a contrite heart (Psalm 51:17) and a meek and quiet spirit (1 Peter 3:4). The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him (Psalm 147:11). He desires the sacrifice of praise and thanks. O worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness (Psalm 96:9).

When will mankind learn that God is not worshiped with things we can see and touch? To offer God things; to build buildings; to set up images, shrines and candles; to wear pins, crosses, or medals; to keep days; to go through ceremonies; to join organizations; to say words—these are not worship. Read Matthew 4:10; Matthew 15:8-9. One sin of idolatry is in belittling God to the littleness of things we can make and acts we can do. True worship is to the true and living God and from the heart. All else is idolatry.
God's Mighty Power

Acts 17:26-29 God made of one blood all nations. All people are brothers physically and in nature. There was but one creation of people. God made Adam, and all descended from him. Also, man is not related to the animal creation (1 Corinthians 15:39). God hath determined the times. He planned the dispensations, the time of the Law, the time for Christ to come, the time for the Judgment, and so it will be. He has set the bonds of man's habitation—where he is to live, and how long, and his powers. It is all to the end that men should seek and find the Lord. The Godhead cannot be likened unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device. He is the Supreme Being, and we are His offspring.
Repentance and the Judgment

Acts 17:30-34 The times of this ignorance God winked at—He looked over idolatry when the people were ignorant, before the Gospel was proclaimed. But now—now Christ has come and died and risen. Now God commandeth . . . to repent— to turn from idolatries and all sins. Why? Because he hath appointed a day, in which he will judge the world. How? In righteousness. Nothing will be hidden. No one will get by with wrong. All will be judged justly by Jesus Christ. Christ is now our Mediator, and then He will be our Judge.

Oh, how the people needed these Truths! Oh, how they needed Christ! They listened until Paul spoke of the Resurrection. Then they drew back. Some mocked and others said, We will hear thee again. Their unbelief shut the door to true knowledge, not in the head, but in the heart. Some believed and entered the ranks of the redeemed. Two are named: Dionysius and Damaris.
JUST A THOUGHT
When someone says he doesn't feel as near to God as he once did, you can be sure which one has moved.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 10
PAUL'S WORK IN CORINTH
Scripture Text: Acts 18:1-23

"After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth." Later on, Silas and Timothy joined him. His labors had been very trying at Athens. Stoned at Lystra and dragged out of the city for dead, Paul was roused to greater vigor. Scourged at Philippi, he and Silas were cast into prison, where they sang praise to God at midnight. But at Athens no one had the least intention of persecuting the Apostle. They simply laughed at him. Thus Paul went out from them. And well he might, for Athens had shut the door on the Gospel.

Corinth was the busiest city in the Roman Empire and the wickedest. Paul had failed in Athens. How could he ever expect to succeed in Corinth? While there, Paul met Aquila and Priscilla, tentmakers who shared Paul's craft. The Lord encouraged Paul in a vision. Insurrection against Paul came to naught.
MEMORY VERSE: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak and hold not thy peace. —Acts 18:9
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Ephesians 1:1-14 Eternal purpose of God.
Tue.—John 5:22-47 Unbelievers rebuked.
Wed.—John 12:37-50 The cause of unbelief.
Thu.—Romans 12:9-21 The new man is forgiving.
Fri.—Hebrews 12:1-13 Chastening and love of the Lord.
Devotional Reading: 1 Corinthians 9:1-18 Support the pastor.
Pressed in the Spirit

Acts 18:1-8 In Corinth Paul found Aquila and his wife Priscilla, Jews lately come from Italy because Claudius Caesar had expelled Jews from Rome. We read of them in Romans 16:3. They were tentmakers as was Paul, so worked together. This was Paul's means of supporting himself. Every Sabbath Paul reasoned in the synagogue. Then Silas and Timothy arrived. Paul was pressed in the spirit. Something within Paul was pressing him to do what he could to fill the needs before him. Obeying God's leading, Paul testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ—the anointed Son of God. This point, more than any other, the Jews objected to. This is the vital point that must be believed to bring salvation (John 8:24). The Jews set themselves against the doctrine. They blasphemed—denied this Truth. Claiming that Christ is only a man is blasphemy. Paul shook his raiment—a gesture of abandonment. Your blood be upon your own heads—bear the responsibility, reap the results, take your own punishment. I am clean—am not responsible for the results of your rejection. The reason Paul could say this was that he had given the people the Gospel. He had told them plainly who Christ is and what He would do for them. He could do no more. As he had often done before, Paul turned to the Gentiles. Many Gentiles believed, and were baptized.

LESSON 10
Encouraged by a Vision

Acts 18:9-11 In love and to encourage and direct, God sent a night vision to Paul. He said, Be not afraid . . . For I am with thee. Jesus told him to fearlessly teach and promised to be with him, that no man shall . . . hurt thee. Jesus had many people there who would believe if they heard. Paul stayed on and continued teaching.

As we look at the life of Paul, we learn that he did not consider the things he suffered as hurt. Should a word of ridicule, a little inconvenience seem to us as persecution? Everyone who does anything, even of a worldly nature, has problems and hardships. So it is in living the life of a Christian. We should ignore small irritations and bear patiently real persecution for our Lord and the greatest cause in the world.

God could see in the persecutor Saul the possible Apostle Paul. He can see in low, wicked sinners possible redeemed, holy saints. He has people in our communities whose salvation depends upon our telling them of Jesus Christ.
We must be obedient to the Spirit of God and tell others that they, too, can be saved. We will be so happy for those who take heed.
Insurrection Against Paul

Acts 18:12-17 The Jews, in fury, raised a disorderly mob and accused Paul before the deputy, Gallio, of teaching to worship contrary to the Law. Paul taught a doctrine that was not contrary to the Law, but was the fulfillment of the Law (Matthew 5:17). It went beyond the Law. It was the reality of which the Law was the shadow (Hebrews 10:1-10). He taught that the ceremonies of the Law were no longer binding and were powerless to save (Acts 13:39), but that Jesus Christ saves repentant sinners. The deputy would not even listen to their accusation and drove them from the judgment seat.
Going to Ephesus

Acts 18:18-23 Still, Paul stayed on a good while. Then bidding farewell to the church, he, Priscilla, and Aquila sailed to Syria, then to Ephesus, where Priscilla and Aquila remained. After reasoning with the Jews there for a short time, Paul went on by way of Caesarea to a feast in Jerusalem. From there, he spent some time in Antioch, teaching and refreshing the saints. Then he traveled on, strengthening all the disciples in the churches in Galatia and Phrygia.

Paul was a true pastor. He fed his flock. He planned to nourish, teach, and encourage them to keep them spiritually healthy and growing. He felt he had accomplished nothing unless his converts continued saved to the end.
JUST A THOUGHT
The value of salvation lies not in what we give up but in what we gain.

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 11
THE SWORD OF THE SPIRIT AT EPHESUS
Scripture Text: Acts 18:24-28; Acts 19:1-12

After Paul left Ephesus and was traveling among the churches, Brother Apollos came to Ephesus. He knew only the baptism of John. Priscilla and Aquila taught him the way of the Lord. When returning to Ephesus, Paul found the Ephesians had not heard of the Holy Spirit. He taught that Jesus promised more than repentance. Twelve men were baptized and Spirit filled. Paul taught the Word of the Lord, and God did special miracles. The disciples worked in harmony with the common purpose of bringing people to the Lord.

Ephesus, about which we study today, was a center of superstition, magic, and satanic arts in the Roman Empire. This week we find Paul in Ephesus striving to lead people out of the darkness of superstition into the light of Christ's Gospel.
MEMORY VERSE: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. —Ephesians 6:10
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 14:15-24 The promise of the Spirit.
Tue.—John 14:25-31 The promise of peace.
Wed.—John 15:1-17 Branches depend fully on the vine.
Thu.—Ezekiel 36:22-32 God to regather Israel.
Fri.—John 6:35-51 Close working of the Father and Son.
Devotional Reading: Romans 6:1-14 Believers, dead to sin.
Apollos Learns More

Acts 18:24-28 Apollos was a talented, eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures . . . instructed in the way of the Lord . . . fervent in the spirit and diligent. Yet his teaching fell short because he knew only the baptism of John. He could go no further in his teaching. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him preaching in the synagogue, they saw a lack in Apollos. They took him privately and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly. They opened to him the way of God further than the baptism of John. They taught him of the baptism of the Holy Spirit. The power of the Holy Spirit in one's heart is the greatest power in the world. Apollos left for Achaia with a letter of commendation from the disciples. There he helped the believers, teaching them his newfound Truth. He effectively taught them that Jesus is the Christ.

John the Baptist was the forerunner of Jesus (Matthew 3; Mark 1; Luke 3). He preached, Repent ye. John said, I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. To have one's sins forgiven requires the blood of Jesus. All of us must have it. This was not enough. John kept pointing ahead to something greater. The kingdom of heaven is at hand . . . One mightier than I cometh . . . He shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.

SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 11
Baptized in the Name of Jesus

Acts 19:1-7 Then Paul, interested in the progress of the disciples, asked, Have ye received the Holy Ghost? No, they had not even heard of Him. Apollos had not told them of the Holy Ghost. Paul asked, Unto what then were ye baptized? Baptism has meaning. What did theirs mean? They were baptized unto John's baptism. Apollos had taught them as far as he knew, but it was not deep enough.

Paul explained that John . . . baptized with the baptism of repentance, but that he pointed ahead to more than that, to belief in Christ Jesus. The people believed and accepted Paul's teaching. They were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They opened their hearts and received the power that only the Holy Spirit gives. The Holy Ghost came on them. God thus witnesses His approval. Immediately the Holy Spirit in the twelve men was active. He helped them to speak with tongues and to prophesy—give messages from God with unlearned languages.

Then Jesus came (Mark 1:14-15). He came preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God. He said, The time is fulfilled. The kingdom is the rule of God within hearts (Luke 17:21). Jesus still preached, Repent ye, but He added, and believe the gospel—the good news that God would live in man. Jesus said, If a man love me . . . we will come unto him, and make our abode with him (John 14:23. They (plural) came in the Person of the Holy Spirit. Jesus said, I will send him unto you (John 16:7). When this is done, the Kingdom of God is set up in that heart.
The Two Baptisms Compared

John preached the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. Later Paul wrote (Romans 6:3-11) of (1) being baptized into Jesus Christ, which is far better. (2) Being baptized into his death, death to sin, separation from sin, and (3) being raised up in the likeness of his resurrection . . . alive unto God through Jesus Christ. Jesus' baptism includes John's. John's baptism signifies repentance. Jesus' baptism signifies this and also the filling with the Holy Spirit.

These twelve disciples were devout men. They had made public repentance of their sin. They had been baptized according to the teaching of John the Baptist. Still, there was something lacking in their lives. They did not have joy, hope, and power—the things which faith in Christ brings to one's experience. They had received the baptism by water, but not the baptism by the Spirit. Paul's message was repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ (Acts 20:21).
Special Miracles

Acts 19:8-12 For three months Paul reasoned in the synagogue concerning the kingdom of God. But when some were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them. He separated the disciples from the unbelievers. To reject Truth has a hardening effect upon the soul, and unbelief locks out the way of light into the life.

Here we have described a fruitful ministry and a mighty spiritual conflict. Paul reasoned and persuaded. The battle he confronted was that of ignorance and superstition, principalities and powers—agents promising help to men but instead destroying their souls. There are angels of light, and there are angels of darkness. God uses heavenly messengers; Satan uses demons. Paul continued for two years to preach until all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word.

God worked in unusual power through Paul at this time. Handkerchiefs and aprons he had touched were carried to the sick and the diseases departed from them. They were carried to the demon possessed, and the evil spirits went out of them.

Paul found a city in bondage to Satan. Paul's work was to transfer the allegiance of these people from Satan to Christ, from darkness to light, from reliance upon superstition to abiding faith in the Truth of the Gospel.

lessons.title: THE SWORD OF THE SPIRIT AT EPHESUS

blocks.text: SUNDAY SCHOOL MATERIALS FOR ADULTS
LESSON 12
IN THE NAME OF JESUS
Scripture Text: Acts 19:13-22
The purity of spiritual life and the power of God were so visible in the Ephesian church that the unsaved desired to imitate.

To sign another's name to a check is forgery and a crime. It is an attempt to obtain the money of another from the bank without depositing one's own money. In our lesson today we learn about exorcists who wished to gain the benefits of Christ without commitment to Him or contact with Him. Their use of His name was forgery. It was taking God's name in vain. It is to His people only that Jesus says, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you (John 16:23).
MEMORY VERSE: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye? —Acts 19:15
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Luke 4:31-39 Unclean spirits and sickness subject.
Tue.—Jude 1:5-23 Doom of false teachers.
Wed.—Hebrews 7:15-28 Superiority of Christ's priesthood.
Thu.—Ezekiel 33:10-20 The message of righteousness.
Fri.—John 10:1-18 Christ the Shepherd of the sheep.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 6:10-20 Whole armor of God.
Exorcists Use Jesus' Name

Acts 19:13-14 God was using Paul in healing the sick and casting out evil spirits. In Ephesus were exorcists—ones who attempt to drive out evil spirits by use of a holy name or by magic rites, or who summon evil spirits by magical formulae. They took upon them—assumed without authority—to call over demon-possessed people the name of the Lord Jesus. They used Christ's name to command His power. Among the exorcists were seven brothers. Their father, Sceva, was a chief priest and should have taught his sons better. Not all who use Jesus' name are His people or have the Truth. To rightly use Jesus' name, we must have contact with God, and must have been born into His family by a new, spiritual birth.
Evil Spirit Answers

Acts 19:15-16 The evil spirit answered—the spirit talked, not the man. Not having a body, he used the man's mouth. Evil spirits can live in and control people. Just as God must have our hands, feet, and mouths to use for His work, so does Satan use human instruments to accomplish his work. Jesus I know, and Paul I know . . . The devil and his spirits are intelligent and have greater insight than humans have. They knew Jesus (Luke 4:41). This one knew Jesus and Paul— probably had been watching and fearing their work. . . . but who are ye? He knew the power of Jesus and Paul. These men had none. The man, moved by the evil spirit, leaped on them, and completely overcame them. The man, demon possessed, was stronger physically than seven men in their own strength.

What was wrong in the action of Sceva's sons? They used Jesus' name against the demon as Paul had done. Why did they fail? (1) Because they had no contact with Jesus. Since He was not present in them, His name was not theirs to use. (2) While they may have appeared to do as Paul, there was a vast difference. It is not the use of
