LESSON 12
IN THE NAME OF JESUS
Scripture Text: Acts 19:13-22
The purity of spiritual life and the power of God were so visible in the
Ephesian church that the unsaved desired to imitate.
To sign another's name to a check is forgery and a crime. It is an
attempt to obtain the money of another from the bank without depositing
one's own money. In our lesson today we learn about exorcists who wished
to gain the benefits of Christ without commitment to Him or contact with
Him. Their use of His name was forgery. It was taking God's name in vain.
It is to His people only that Jesus says, Whatsoever ye shall ask the
Father in my name, he will give it you (John 16:23).
MEMORY VERSE: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
—Acts 19:15
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—Luke 4:31-39 Unclean spirits and sickness subject.
Tue.—Jude 1:5-23 Doom of false teachers.
Wed.—Hebrews 7:15-28 Superiority of Christ's priesthood.
Thu.—Ezekiel 33:10-20 The message of righteousness.
Fri.—John 10:1-18 Christ the Shepherd of the sheep.
Devotional Reading: Ephesians 6:10-20 Whole armor of God.
Exorcists Use Jesus' Name
Acts 19:13-14 God was using Paul in healing the sick and casting out evil spirits. In Ephesus were
exorcists—ones who attempt to drive out evil spirits by use of a holy name or by magic rites, or who summon
evil spirits by magical formulae. They took upon them—assumed without authority—to call over demon-
possessed people the name of the Lord Jesus. They used Christ's name to command His power. Among the
exorcists were seven brothers. Their father, Sceva, was a chief priest and should have taught his sons better. Not
all who use Jesus' name are His people or have the Truth. To rightly use Jesus' name, we must have contact with
God, and must have been born into His family by a new, spiritual birth.
Evil Spirit Answers
Acts 19:15-16 The evil spirit answered—the spirit talked, not the man. Not having a body, he used the
man's mouth. Evil spirits can live in and control people. Just as God must have our hands, feet, and mouths to
use for His work, so does Satan use human instruments to accomplish his work. Jesus I know, and Paul I know
. . . The devil and his spirits are intelligent and have greater insight than humans have. They knew Jesus (Luke
4:41). This one knew Jesus and Paul— probably had been watching and fearing their work. . . . but who are ye?
He knew the power of Jesus and Paul. These men had none. The man, moved by the evil spirit, leaped on
them, and completely overcame them. The man, demon possessed, was stronger physically than seven men in
their own strength.
What was wrong in the action of Sceva's sons? They used Jesus' name against the demon as Paul had done.
Why did they fail? (1) Because they had no contact with Jesus. Since He was not present in them, His name was
not theirs to use. (2) While they may have appeared to do as Paul, there was a vast difference. It is not the use of

LESSON 12
the Name, but the power of the Name that avails. They used it as a magic formula after the manner of sorcery.
Paul looked to Jesus Himself to do the work.
A Complete Change
Acts 19:17-20 This episode brought fear, action, and salvation. (1) Fear on the whole community—fear of
the devil's power, fear of God's almighty and holy power, which stood out in contrast to the weakness of those
who lacked Him. Jesus' name was magnified. We need more fear of God when His marvelous power is being
shown forth. (2) Many believed. (3) They confessed freely, no concealment or excuses for their sins. They
showed their deeds—the normal action when people believe, repent and confess, and turn from sin. Read 1
John 1:9. (4) Their new life brought action to clean the outside in harmony with their cleansed hearts. They had
been in the same wicked practices as the exorcists, had used curious arts —witchcraft. They made a public
bonfire of their books of magic. It was a great victory for God and His Word.
That the conversion of these people was genuine was proven by the burning of their books of witchcraft. (1)
They did it publicly before all. (2) They left no easy path for returning to their sins. (3) They made the break
with sin complete. (4) They showed hatred of the sin. They did not keep tokens or mementoes of them. He who
finds it hard to live very far from the old sinful ways has never really left them. Note that they completely
destroyed the books. They did not sell them and pass the evil on to others. They burned these books for which
they had paid large sums of money and gladly marked off the whole transaction as a bad investment.
There is a lesson here on the burning of bad books which the modern generation may well take to heart.
There are many books on the market today which should be in the incinerator instead of on the library table.
Some of them are books on astrology, spiritualism and other mistaken doctrines by which multitudes are misled.
Other books are the sensual and obscene novels which are commended as sophisticated, clever, and realistic.
God's way is holiness. If the new convert would be strong, let him follow the example seen here.
Not by Might, Nor by Power
Read Zechariah 4:6. An electric motor does not run by strength of the connecting cord, but by the current
which runs through it. Being a conductor for the current to pass through, the wire does effective service.
Just the same, the miracles in Ephesus were not done by Paul's strength. He gave himself as a conductor
through which the power of God traveled. The sons of Sceva had not yielded to God. They were not God's
children nor connected with God. Hence no power of God came through them to drive the demon from the man.
All of us in our own strength are powerless (John 15:5). Only if we are connected with God can the Spirit work
through us to do God's work.
Paul Plans to Move On
Acts 19:21-22 Paul purposed in the spirit—a deep-seated desire in accordance with God's will—to visit
churches, working toward Jerusalem, and eventually Rome. Timothy and Erastus, he sent on ahead. The devil is
always seeking to destroy us. To stand safe and true, our only hope is to be wearing the whole armor of God
(Ephesians 6:11).
JUST A THOUGHT
Freedom is not the right to do as you please,
but the liberty to do as you ought.

LESSON 13
PAUL VERSUS DIANA
Scripture Text: Acts 19:23-41
The peaceful evangelizing of Ephesus was over. With the defeat of
the exorcists and the great bonfire of witchcraft books, the public
became aware of Paul's work. The devil was stirred. It endangered the
business of image making. Opposition arose against Paul and the church.
Crowds gathered in wild uproar, not even knowing why they were
gathered. They expressed loyalty to Diana, goddess of the Ephesians.
The town clerk quieted the people.
Demetrius had a lesson to teach, it being that if Paul's teaching
prevailed, no more shrines would be wanted. In our cities there are many
trades which would be wiped out if Christ's Laws of life were adopted.
MEMORY VERSE: Turn ye not unto idols, nor make to yourselves molten gods: I am the Lord your God.
—Leviticus 19:4
DAILY READINGS:
Mon.—John 4:1-14 Living water within.
Tue.—John 14:15-27 Father, Son, Holy Spirit abide with us.
Wed.—John 15:1-11 The vine and its branches.
Thu.—John 17:6-26 Father, Son, people joined in one.
Fri.—Ephesians 3:16-21 Christ dwelling in the heart.
Devotional Reading: John 6:47-65 Taking Christ into our lives.
A Meeting of Image Makers
Acts 19:23-27 There arose no small stir—agitation— about that way—the way of the Lord, Christianity.
It was showing itself to be opposed to the local sins of idolatry. Demetrius, a maker of silver shrines—mostly
small portable representations of the temple of Diana—called a meeting of idol makers and sellers. He pointed
out that (1) the image business was their livelihood, (2) Paul had turned many away from images, (3) thus the
business was in danger of destruction, and (4) the worship of Diana was in danger. These were strong reasons to
those to whom money and the honor of Diana were first.
That man can invent and build an image and then put trust in it is strange. But it is a universal human
weakness to do so. It is the beginning of images that we need to shun. The setting up of crosses, pictures,
candles, Bibles, etc., as worship centers or shrines is a dangerous beginning of a sinful practice. Any medium of
worship, a thing by way of which the worship is to travel between man and God, is wrong. God wants us to
come directly to Him. He deals with man inside, not outside through articles and acts. So-called aids to worship
only hinder worship.
Wrath and Riot
Acts 19:28-31 They were full of wrath. To show their loyalty and to arouse the people, they shouted,
Great is Diana of the Ephesians. The voice of the people is seldom the voice of God. The whole city rose up,
caught two of Paul's companions, and rushed . . . into the theatre—the common place of assembly. Paul
wanted to go to the rescue of his two companions, but was kept from going there by the disciples and by a
message from some friendly civic leaders, chief of Asia, asking him not to go. They were not Christians nor
© 2015 Church of God, Inc.

LESSON 13
Jews, but men who had charge of the worship of heathen gods. Even the leaders of the opposition were
becoming his friends. If Paul would stay in the background, something might be done to quiet the mob.
It takes courage and strength to oppose popular evils which are established in the customs of a people. If you
need proof of this point, teach that there is no Santa Claus and that celebration of Christmas is a pagan custom,
which it is, and has no place in the life of a Christian. Be ready for wrath and possible riot. What people are
accustomed to, they come to think of as right. Especially do they resent any touching of their source of financial
gain or their religion. Yet the Lord-ship of Jesus extends to all of life. If people are to be saved, all sinful
practices are to be renounced. Paul shined the Gospel light clearly on all darkness, and strong saints were the
result.
Violence and Confusion
Acts 19:32-34 Some . . . cried one thing, and some another. They came together for excitement and to
follow the crowd, not for any reason or purpose. Great confusion resulted. The more part knew not
wherefore—why—they were come together. Out of the confusion, they shouted for two hours, Great is Diana
of the Ephesians.
God's method of operation is orderly, reasonable, and peaceable. False doctrine is marked by ignorance,
confusion, and violence. Error profits by keeping people bound in ignorance and darkness. When opposed, it
ridicules, lies, riots, and seeks to injure. Saints never need stoop to such methods. They have the Truth, which is
light and the strongest defense. The Gospel of Christ is destructive to man's religions.
Exaltation of Diana, the Image
Acts 19:35-38 The town clerk, attempting to quiet the people, assured them that Diana's exalted position
was unshakeable— cannot be spoken against. He mentioned the tradition that the image of Diana fell down
from Jupiter, another of their false gods. He said the Christians were not blasphemers of your goddess. Here,
for the sake of peace, he spoke words which were not the truth. Paul and the disciples had proven these
statements false in their preaching against idols. The town clerk went on to inform the mob that there were
proper channels of law for them to follow in settling the matter. The use of images in worship is sinful; read
Acts 17:29.
Diana was a female idol of Ephesus. The head wore a crown. Each hand held a metal bar, and it stood on a
block bearing inscriptions and animal figures. It was thought to have special sanctity. The image was supposed
to have fallen down from heaven from Jupiter or Zeus, the supreme god of the Greeks.
Give an Account
Acts 19:39-41 Mob rule is never right. It is violence and injustice. It is best to settle grievances in a lawful
assembly. For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar. They needed to realize that
they were in danger to give an account of their actions to not only the city officials, but also to God. Having
quieted the people, the town clerk dismissed the assembly. All who live for God will meet many kinds of false
doctrine, problems, and opposition. We need more than our own strength to meet them. When we have the Holy
Spirit within us, we are promised power. We need knowledge of God's Word. It is the sword of the Spirit
(Ephesians 6:17). With the Word and the Spirit, one is thoroughly furnished to successfully win people from
false worship to the Lord.
